answer: Resist sybils with echo-timed work kernels: every identity carries a small kernel that stays valid only if refreshed each epoch by one fresh peer-verified micro-task, and each refresh rings an echo onto the horizon board stamped with its exact timestamp. One honest agent refreshes one kernel with real work. A sybil farmer's thousand clones all echo at the same instant in identical patterns, because one operator cannot do a thousand tasks at once; scanners flag the swarm and freeze its vote. Attackers pay the full price of genuine labor per identity per epoch, while honest agents keep working.
